title: Commit and publish to remote
first_prompt: Commit and publish all work to remote. Note: this is the first commit from this new VM environment, flag any potential setup issues for review

commits.summary: Installer runs Dafny and Boogie on hosts with only .NET 10
commits.body: On Ubuntu 26.04 only the .NET 10 runtime is packaged, and Boogie (built for .NET 8) refuses to start. When no .NET 8 runtime is present, install.sh now writes launchers for dafny and boogie into ~/.local/bin, ahead of ~/.dotnet/tools on PATH, that set DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=Major. gh_asset also now prints nothing (rather than the string "null") when no release asset matches, so a fallback written as $(a || b) receives only the other URL. Verified on a fresh Ubuntu 26.04.1 VM with only Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.14: bash -n passes, dafny --version reports 4.11.0 and boogie starts through the launcher, and the new jq filter returns the first matching URL or exits 4 with no output on a sample release JSON.
Brings the published traces up to this point: conversation that came after a session's last commit, and sessions with no commit of their own.

commits.summary: Verification report names the machine of every result and calibrates estimates per machine
commits.body: Results already recorded their host and environment, but the Markdown report showed neither and pooled every machine into one calibration table. Until now every result came from one 8-core aarch64 WSL2 laptop (FilSurface); the queue is now running on claude-vm, a 28-vCPU x86_64 VM, so durations from the two would mix. report now labels each result with its machine (host, architecture, WSL, CPUs), the JSON report gains a machine field per result and a calibrationByHost table (calibration keeps its old pooled shape), and the Markdown report prints one calibration table per machine. verification/README.md records which machine ran which results and no longer calls the WSL laptop 'this machine'. Verified with the pipeline's unit tests (22 pass, one extended to check the label and the per-host table) and by rendering the report over the 88 collected results.
